title: Rabbi Chana
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Ketubot 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.61a.8): “Rabbi Chana said — and some say Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani — she did not literally bring in to him,” etc. Likewise in Bava Kamma 51a as cited by Hyman,[^3] “Rabbi Chana said — and some say Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani — what is the meaning of what is written, ‘long-suffering’?” etc. (In [Eruvin 22a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.22a.6) the reading is Rabbi Chaggai.) Hyman considers this Rabbi Chana likely to have been a Palestinian, and he is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Sotah 7:7: “Rabbi Chanah, Rabbi Yirmeyah in the name of Rabbi Chiyya (bar Abba).”[^2]

notes.text: The supplied Rabbi Chana is retained against saved Davidson Ketubot 61a’s full Rav Chana. The alternative attribution to Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani remains. Sotah 7:7 is Jerusalem Talmud, and the Palestinian identity inference is Hyman’s.

The consulted Ketubot has Rav Chana. The linked Eruvin has Rabbi Chaggai in the slow-to-anger interpretation, with Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani as the alternative. Hyman’s Bava Kamma locator and identification remain as supplied.

The attribution to Rabbi Chana, with Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani as the alternative, is at the end of [Bava Kamma 50a:23](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.50a.23). At the start of [Bava Kamma 50b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.50b.1), the plural expression “long-suffering” is applied to both the righteous and the wicked.
